evidence.quote: qui omnes ... in duas partes discedunt: ab altera parte stat unus codex Bruxellensis, ab altera ceteri omnes.
Iam declaravimus non solum L et T ex codice V haustos esse, sed etiam praeter B omnes.
explorato autem omnes Ennodi codices in duas partes distribuendos esse, quarum altera uno efficitur codice B, altera V, ceterorum omnium capite
Statuimus igitur codicem B ex ipso archetypo descriptum esse
hoc codicum stemmate illustrentur: [diagram garbled: 'X fortasse Pseudo-Isidorus' ... B ... V ... L ... T C P]

texts.notes: Two branches: B alone vs V and all its descendants (L copied from V; T, C, P from a later apograph of V; O allied to L; C and P share an exemplar that often agrees with T but is not derived from T). Pseudo-Isidore drew on an exemplar of the V class older than V (indirect). The printed stemma on p. XLVIII is garbled; check the image for the exact placement of O, C, P and of the lost intermediate (X) between archetype and V.
